text:
Taylor Reed: quick triage note: canary observed a small but steady 'active_sessions' drift after clients hit a noisy proxy that returns 204 on half-close. UI shows tenants with slowly increasing active_token_seconds even after clients reconnect.
Priya Menon: Can you repro?
Taylor Reed: Yeah: client opens WS, proxy returns 204 on FIN, client reconnects (new socket) -> new session accepted, old session stays counted because we never see EOF. Happens ~1-2% of reconnects in canary under load.
Gabe Ortiz: Do we have a tombstone/lease for sessions?
Taylor Reed: We do, but current tombstone TTL=30s and the GC path is noisy under high churn. Also routing sometimes accepts resume on different shard and both increment optimistic quota counters.
Anya Kuznetsova: Console UX: ops pages show per-route active_sessions and per-tenant billing graph. This drift triggers paging rules. We need either a backend fix or a safe UI smoothing so SREs aren't woken at 3am.
Priya Menon: Backend proposals: a) reduce tombstone TTL to 5s (fast GC) b) make accept do an atomic claim in routing-metadata (slower) c) keep optimistic accept + async reconcile that emits compensating events if CAS fails.
Gabe Ortiz: d) add an admin eviction API so humans can force-GC a stuck resume_id during emergency.
Taylor Reed: I'm in favor of (c) + (d). Keep latency on accept low, but ensure billing pipeline can correct via compensating events. Admin API for emergencies.
Anya Kuznetsova: For the console, can we do non-destructive smoothing: show a "suspected-stale" overlay and suppress alerts for those reconciling windows?
Priya Menon: Yes. Implementation: console aggregation dedupe by (tenant,resume_id) for 60s, mark as "reconciling" and link to metric. Add a flag to re-enable strict alerts if needed.
Gabe Ortiz: Telemetry: add metric stream_resume_leak_detected (tag shard, tenant, route) and stream_resume_reconcile_emitted. Also log claim_nonce on accept: `claim_nonce=0x4f2a` to correlate events.
Taylor Reed: Example logs to produce so we can match spans:
```
INFO 2031-02-10T07:12:01Z accept resume_id=rm_9c8 shard=ap-south-1 last_event=512 claim_nonce=0x4f2a span=trace-12ab
WARN 2031-02-10T07:12:01Z reconcile conflict resume_id=rm_9c8 shard=ap-south-2 winner_nonce=0x4f2a loser_nonce=0x7b3d
```
Priya Menon: Billing pipeline needs to consume `quota_compensation` events. We should attach tenant_id, resume_id, reason=duplicate_claim. Also record original increment timestamp so meter can roll back correctly.
Gabe Ortiz: Routing tweak idea: soft affinity routing that prefers the shard that last renewed the resume_id if last_seen < 10s. No strong consistency, just reduces cross-shard accepts.
Anya Kuznetsova: UX plan: add a transient banner on tenant billing page: "Possible duplicate resume activity detected — reconciling. Alerts muted for this window." Link goes to reconcile metric and the admin-evict docs.
Taylor Reed: Admin API sketch for emergency evict:
```
POST /admin/v1/resume/rm_9c8/evict?force=true
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <op-token>
Response: 200 {"evicted":true, "corrected_quota": 120}
```
Priya Menon: Need idempotent semantics and audit log for this. Good to add `dry_run=true` param for safety.
Gabe Ortiz: Deploy plan: ship async-reconciler worker + metric + claim_nonce logs -> canary in ap-south in 30m. Console dedupe behind feature flag and set false by default until ops validates.
deploy-bot: Rolling: async-reconciler worker -> ap-south canary queued.
ops-bot: Created INF-9992: "streaming: async reconcile + console smoothing (dedupe 60s)" assigned to Anya. ETA 4d.
Taylor Reed: Action items: 1) PR for async reconcile + quota_compensation event (Gabe) 2) claim_nonce logs + metric (Gabe/Priya) 3) admin evict API spec (Priya) 4) console smoothing feature flag + banner (Anya) 5) canary monitor for stream_resume_leak_detected (ops).
Anya Kuznetsova: I'll implement console change non-destructively (only UI suppression) and surface raw numbers in an advanced view.
Priya Menon: Also add a reconciler span and a dashboard chart for reconcile latency — useful to see how long compensations take to flow to the billing pipeline.
Taylor Reed: Great. I'll post canary telemetry once it's live. Thanks all :thumbsup:
